Now that I am officially part of the voat CFB poll, i figured i would explain my ranking format again....expect to see this post linked to my ranking every week when i post it.

FIRST: a historical discussion on my ranking. I have been playing with ranking formulas for about 12 years now. I have tried several statistical models over the years and I have discovered a philosophical issue. Should a ranking be used to predict outcomes and determine the "best" team, or should a ranking be used to examine what you have accomplished and determine the most "deserving" team? back when i started my rankings I was a hard supporter of the "best" team answer. but over the years, you start to see things that don't work with ranking the "best" team philosophy. many head to head matchups appear to be ignored. Oh...Michigan State beat Ohio State head to head....screw you! OSU is still calculated as 4.5 points better than MSU, so MSU can kiss my shiny metal butt!!!!

I had tried to balance the 2 for a while. putting in margin of victory caps, over-weighting record, etc. finally 2 years ago I decided to completely remove score altogether from my spreadsheet. the only thing that matters is what is your record, and who you beat. This makes the spreadsheet far LESS valuable as a prediction tool, but far more valuable in ranking the most worthy teams (IMHO).

so this is my current formula (and has been the formula for the last 2 seasons)

FIRST...games against 1AA teams are scrubbed from your record (unless you lose). you don't get credit for beating a team with 30 fewer scholarship players. so no...even if you played NDSU, that game still doesn't count (unless you lose)

SECOND...the basic formula is this: (team's winning %) x (team's strength of schedule)...that's it

THIRD...the SOS formula I use is the same as what the BCS used in it's 1999 version of its formula. that explanation can be found HERE (skip the part where it talks about quartiles, i don't need or use that) it is basically a modified version of (2 x opponents record + opponent's opponents's record) / 3. this is a nearly identical formula as the published basketball RPI SOS. So there is a long standing historical backing to this as a SOS formula.

and...that's it. your record times your strength of schedule. i don't care if you eek out a 1 point win in every game or blow everyone out by 50. a win is a win is a win.

so Ruston. How do you plan on doing a preseaon ranking?

well...the only thing less useful than a preseason raking is a preseason COMPUTER ranking. but just for grins and giggles I decided to justify something.

so i took the final RPR ranking of each team from last year and used that as my predictor. if you had a higher RPR than your opponent, you are predicted to win that game. if you have a lower RPR, you are expected to lose. generate an expected result from every game, and use that as your preseason ranking.

But won't that mess up the rankings after week 1?

nope...the preseason rankings will be dumped into the memory hole after week 1. that data will have no impact on any future rankings. i don't use predictors in my rankings (expect for the preseason ranking) so that data is nothing more than a fun time waster for me. what WILL mess with the week 1 rankings is the fact that everyone will be either 1-0, 0-1, or 0-0 (for those opening with a 1AA team). I have actually never run a ranking on week 1, so I may end up with a lot of Divide by 0 errors. normally i wait until week 6 before i start running the numbers. we will see.

I hope this will counterbalance my system of gut instinct+butthurt+littlebrotherhatred-potbangingsunshine/OUsux formula.
